en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on the Crossed Legs.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one sitting with his legs folded under him...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is sitting with his legs folded under him.
One who is not ill and is sitting with his legs folded under him should not be taught the Dhamma.

Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is sitting with his hands folded over his knees or with his robe folded over his knees, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional … [and so forth] …
"For one who is a first offender":
thus ends the fifth training rule.
